proposals.before: The emperor praised his integrity and raised Feng's rank to grand coachman of the imperial household.
proposals.after: The emperor praised his integrity and raised Feng's rank to Grandee of Splendid Light.
proposals.reason: 光祿大夫 is Grandee of Splendid Light / palace grandee, not grand coachman of the imperial household.

proposals.before: The emperor praised his integrity and added Feng's rank to grand coachman of the imperial household.
proposals.after: The emperor praised his integrity and added Feng's rank as Grandee of Splendid Light.
proposals.reason: 光祿大夫 is Grandee of Splendid Light / palace grandee, not grand coachman of the imperial household.

proposals.before: Your Majesty did not measure your subject's ability yet appointed him metropolitan governor; he has had no way to prove himself, and you again raised your subject to grand coachman—office is lofty and responsibility heavy; it is not what your subject should hold.
proposals.after: Your Majesty did not measure your subject's ability yet appointed him metropolitan governor; he has had no way to prove himself, and you again raised your subject to Grandee of Splendid Light--the office is lofty and responsibility heavy; it is not what your subject should hold.
proposals.reason: 光祿大夫 is Grandee of Splendid Light / palace grandee, not grand coachman.

proposals.before: Fu Shang was the grand empress's half-brother and the nearest kin left.
proposals.after: Fu Shang was a son born of the same womb as the great imperial grandmother's father--her paternal uncle--and the nearest kin left.
proposals.reason: 皇太太后父同產子 means a sibling of the Empress Dowager's father, not the grand empress's half-brother.

proposals.before: The emperor's uncle Wang Li used Li Shang of Nanyang to grab hundreds of qing of marsh and wasteland, then asked the court to pay for it.
proposals.after: The emperor's uncle Wang Li used Li Shang of Nan Commandery to grab hundreds of qing of marsh and wasteland, then asked the court to pay for it.
proposals.reason: 南郡 is Nan Commandery, not Nanyang.

proposals.before: At that time the emperor's maternal uncle, Marquis of Hongyang Wang Li, had retainers acting through Administrator of Nanyang Li Shang seize several hundred qing of reclaimed grassland. Much of it was hillside and marsh that common people had leased from the Privy Treasurer—all was roughly developed—and they memorialized, wishing to turn it over to the commandery treasury.
proposals.after: At that time the emperor's maternal uncle, Marquis of Hongyang Wang Li, had retainers acting through Administrator of Nan Commandery Li Shang seize several hundred qing of reclaimed grassland. Much of it was hillside and marsh that common people had leased from the Privy Treasurer--all was roughly developed--and they memorialized, wishing to turn it over to the commandery treasury.
proposals.reason: 南郡 is Nan Commandery, not Nanyang.

proposals.before: Du Zhiji died the next winter.
proposals.after: Du Zhiji died the next year.
proposals.reason: 明年 means next year here; the literal translation already has this correctly, not next winter.

proposals.before: Later Guangwudi honored the family with a post for his grandson Kang.
proposals.after: In the Jianwu era, recording old virtuous ministers, the court appointed Bao's grandson Kang as a chief.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents "Guangwudi" and omits the Jianwu-era / recording-old-ministers wording present in the Chinese and literal.

proposals.before: It scolded him for haggling with the Fu palace over slave prices.
proposals.after: Long stands among the Nine Ministers yet has not corrected what the court lacks; instead he memorializes to wrangle with the Yongxin Palace over the price of slave-girls, stating it openly in memorials that everyone has heard.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits the edict content and replaces 永信宮 (Yongxin Palace) with the invented gloss “Fu palace.”

proposals.before: When Emperor Ai died and Wang Mang took control of the government, he had Grand Minister of Works Kong Guang memorialize that Long, formerly Shepherd of Ji Province, had handled the Zhongshan Empress Dowager Feng case unjustly and trapped the innocent, and therefore should not hold office in the central region.
proposals.after: When Emperor Ai died and Wang Mang took control of the government, he had Grand Minister over the Masses Kong Guang memorialize that Long, formerly Shepherd of Ji Province, had handled the Zhongshan Empress Dowager Feng case unjustly and trapped the innocent, and therefore should not hold office in the central region.
proposals.reason: Chinese 大司徒 is Grand Minister over the Masses, not Grand Minister of Works (大司空).

proposals.before: When Emperor Ai died, Wang Mang seized government and had Grand Minister of Works Kong Guang memorialize that Long, as former shepherd of Ji Province, had handled the Zhongshan Lady Feng case unjustly and trapped the innocent—he should not hold office in the central plain.
proposals.after: When Emperor Ai died, Wang Mang seized government and had Grand Minister over the Masses Kong Guang memorialize that Long, as former shepherd of Ji Province, had handled the Zhongshan Lady Feng case unjustly and trapped the innocent—he should not hold office in the central plain.
proposals.reason: Chinese 大司徒 is Grand Minister over the Masses, not Grand Minister of Works (大司空).

proposals.before: He Bing's grandfather relocated to Pingling on a clerk's salary.
proposals.after: He Bing, courtesy name Zilian, was a man whose grandfather moved from Pingyu to Pingling as a clerk at two thousand piculs.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits courtesy name 子廉 and the move from 平輿, both present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: He was transferred to governor of Yingchuan, replacing Yan Xu of Lingsyang.
proposals.after: He was transferred to governor of Yingchuan, replacing Yan Xu of Lingyang.
proposals.reason: Place 陵陽 is Lingyang, not Lingsyang.

proposals.before: Later Guangwudi honored a grandson with a gentleman appointment.
proposals.after: In the Jianwu era a grandson of Bing was appointed gentleman.
proposals.reason: Chinese 建武中 names only the Jianwu era; idiomatic invents the temple name Guangwudi.

proposals.before: Chengdi did adopt the Dingtao prince; Long won Ji Province and Yingchuan.
proposals.after: The emperor eventually established the King of Dingtao as crown prince; Long was promoted to Shepherd of Ji Province and Administrator of Yingchuan.
proposals.reason: 立定陶王為太子 means the King of Dingtao was established as crown prince, not adopted; 遷 names Long's two promotions rather than places he 'won.'

proposals.before: Ai made him metropolitan governor, then Bearer of the Mace.
proposals.after: When Emperor Ai took the throne, Long entered the capital as Metropolitan Governor on the strength of his top performance rating, then was promoted to Bearer of the Mace.
proposals.reason: The compressed draft omits 以高第 and leaves Long implicit; the source says his top performance rating led to his capital appointment before his promotion.

proposals.before: Eunuchs hauled ten wagonloads of arsenal weapons to Dong Xian and the nurse Wang.
proposals.after: At the time, Gentleman Attendant Dong Xian was rising in favor. The emperor ordered palace eunuchs to draw weapons from the imperial arsenal in ten successive deliveries and send them to Dong Xian and the household of the emperor's wet nurse, Wang A.
proposals.reason: 前後十輩 means ten successive groups or deliveries, not wagonloads. The source names Dong Xian twice, gives his office and rising favor, and identifies the wet nurse as Wang A.

proposals.before: The privy purse feeds the harem, not the granary budget.
proposals.after: Even the emperor's own maintenance is not paid from the Grand Minister of Agriculture's funds; all expenditures for his support and rewards for service come from the Privy Treasurer.
proposals.reason: The draft replaces the sentence with a loose slogan. The Chinese distinguishes the Grand Minister of Agriculture's public funds from maintenance and reward expenditures paid by the Privy Treasurer.

proposals.before: Keeping granary coin off petty spending was how Han drew the line between palace and state.
proposals.after: This ensures that essential reserves are not spent on incidental uses and the people's labor is not consumed by frivolous expenses; it distinguishes public from private and makes the proper course clear.
proposals.reason: The draft narrows 本藏 and 末用 to granary coin and petty spending and omits the explicit protection of the people's labor.

proposals.before: He traced how axes and arsenal issues were tied to real military duty.
proposals.after: In antiquity, feudal lords and regional commanders empowered to wage punitive campaigns were granted axes and halberds. Han frontier officers charged with repelling raiders likewise receive weapons from the imperial arsenal; in every case, they receive them only after accepting the corresponding duty.
proposals.reason: The source gives the substance of Long's historical analogy; the draft merely summarizes that an analogy occurred and drops its argument.

proposals.before: The Spring and Autumn canon forbade private armor to clip ministerial muscle.
proposals.after: According to the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals, private households may not store armor; this restrains the power of ministers and diminishes their private strength.
proposals.reason: The draft's slangy 'clip ministerial muscle' obscures the explicit rule and its two stated purposes.

proposals.before: He said giving state arms to Dong Xian and a nurse turned public gear into private toys.
proposals.after: Now Dong Xian and the others are merely fawning favorites and insignificant women favored in private, yet the empire's public resources supply their private households, and the state's instruments of military authority equip their families.
proposals.reason: The source continues Long's memorial in direct speech and contrasts public resources and state weapons with private households; 'private toys' is invented and trivializes the charge.

proposals.before: He warned that arming playthings would teach the realm contempt.
proposals.after: The people's labor is diverted to favorites, and weapons of war are furnished to insignificant women. This arrangement is improper: it encourages arrogance and usurpation and sets the wrong example for the realm.
proposals.reason: The draft substitutes a vague summary for the source's concrete parallel clauses and explicit warning about arrogance and usurpation.

proposals.before: He quoted Confucius on the three Huan arsenals.
proposals.after: Confucius said, 'What place has this in the halls of the Three Families?'
proposals.reason: The source quotes Confucius directly and says 三家, the Three Families; it does not mention the Huan clans or arsenals in this sentence.

proposals.before: Confucius said, 'What can be taken from the hall of the three families!
proposals.after: Confucius said, 'What place has this in the halls of the Three Families?'
proposals.reason: 奚取於 asks what place or application something has there; the existing literal is ungrammatical and leaves the quotation unclosed.

proposals.before: Your subject begs to collect the weapons back into the arsenal."
proposals.after: I ask that the weapons be recovered and returned to the arsenal."
proposals.reason: 收還武庫 means to recover the issued weapons and return them to the arsenal; the existing wording is awkward and less precise.

proposals.before: Grand Dowager Fu's buyers underpaid palace women and skimmed Bearer of the Mace maids.
proposals.after: Before long, Empress Dowager Fu had attendants buy slave women from various government offices at cut-rate prices; she also took eight slave women from the office of the Bearer of the Mace.
proposals.reason: 傅太后 is Empress Dowager Fu, not Grand Dowager Fu. The source says her attendants bought government slave women cheaply and separately took eight from Long's office.

proposals.before: Wujiang Long demanded fair prices for the sales.
proposals.after: Long memorialized that the price was too low and requested that a fair value be set.
proposals.reason: The source says Long submitted a memorial reporting that the price was too low and requested revaluation; 'demanded' overstates the action.

proposals.before: The edict called the quarrel vulgar and demoralizing."
proposals.after: His actions do not accord with right principle. From this comes his reputation for wrangling over advantage; he provides no example to the hundred officials and damages moral instruction and custom."
proposals.reason: The draft reduces the edict's full accusation to a vague summary, omitting its claims about improper conduct, reputation, official example, and damaged custom.

decisions.reason: Chinese 光祿大夫 is Grandee of Splendid Light; “grand coachman of the imperial household” mistranslates a different office (太僕), and the proposed replacement is accurate.

decisions.after: The emperor praised his integrity and increased Feng's rank to that of Grandee of Splendid Light.
decisions.reason: 光祿大夫 is Grandee of Splendid Light, not Grand Coachman; 加秩 here increases Feng's rank to that grade.

decisions.after: Your Majesty did not measure your subject's ability yet appointed him metropolitan governor; he has had no way to prove himself, and you again raised your subject to Grandee of Splendid Light—office is lofty and responsibility heavy; it is not what your subject should hold.
decisions.reason: 復秩臣為光祿大夫 requires Grandee of Splendid Light, not grand coachman; keep the original em dash and wording around “office,” changing only the mistranslated title.

decisions.after: Fu Shang, Palace Attendant and Grandee of Splendid Light, was the Imperial Great Empress Dowager's paternal cousin. She had raised him from childhood, and no bond was closer.
decisions.reason: 父同產子 means the son of a full sibling of her father, making Fu Shang her paternal cousin rather than her uncle or half-brother. 小自保大 says she raised him from childhood.

decisions.after: At the time, the emperor's maternal uncle Wang Li, Marquis of Hongyang, had retainers use Nan Commandery Administrator Li Shang's influence to claim several hundred qing of uncultivated land. Much of it was marshland that the Privy Treasurer had leased to commoners and that they had already reclaimed. Wang Li then memorialized offering it to the government.
decisions.reason: 南郡 is Nan Commandery, not Nanyang. The fuller revision also preserves the commoners' prior leases and reclamation, which the draft omitted.

decisions.after: At that time the emperor's maternal uncle, Marquis of Hongyang Wang Li, had retainers use the influence of Li Shang, Administrator of Nan Commandery, to claim several hundred qing of uncultivated land. Much of it consisted of marshland the Privy Treasurer had leased to commoners, nearly all of which had already been reclaimed. Wang Li memorialized, wishing to transfer it to the government.
decisions.reason: 南郡 must be Nan Commandery. The revision also clarifies the retainers' use of Li Shang, the commoners' leases, and 略皆開發.
明年 means the next year; “next winter” invents a season absent from 明年，稚季病死.

decisions.after: During the Jianwu era, when the court honored ministers of former merit, Bao's grandson Kang was appointed magistrate of Zhu.
decisions.reason: The sentence names only the Jianwu era, not Guangwudi. 諸 is Zhu County in Langya and 長 is its magistrate, not a generic chief.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 建武中，錄舊德臣，以寶孫伉為諸長

decisions.after: Long ranks among the Nine Ministers, yet instead of correcting the court's failings, he memorializes to haggle with Yongxin Palace over the price of slave-girls, airing the dispute before everyone.
decisions.reason: The original omits the edict's charge and invents 'Fu palace' for 永信宮. The revision restores Yongxin Palace and condenses the public wrangling into natural English.

decisions.after: When Emperor Ai died and Wang Mang took control of the government, he had Grand Minister over the Masses Kong Guang memorialize that, as former Shepherd of Ji Province, Long had mishandled the case of Empress Dowager Feng of Zhongshan and entrapped innocent people, and therefore should not serve in the central government.
decisions.reason: 大司徒 is Grand Minister over the Masses, not Grand Minister of Works. 中朝 here is the central government, not a geographical region.

decisions.after: When Emperor Ai died, Wang Mang seized control of the government and had Grand Minister over the Masses Kong Guang memorialize that, as former Shepherd of Ji Province, Long had handled the case of Empress Dowager Feng of Zhongshan unjustly and entrapped innocent people; he therefore should not hold office in the central government.
decisions.reason: The literal likewise requires Grand Minister over the Masses for 大司徒, and 中朝 means the central government rather than the central plain.

decisions.after: He Bing, courtesy name Zilian, came from a family whose grandfather had moved from Pingyu to Pingling as a two-thousand-picul official.
decisions.reason: The sentence gives He Bing's courtesy name and his grandfather's move from Pingyu. The revision retains both facts without the draft's awkward 'was a man whose' construction.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 何併字子廉，祖父以吏二千石自平輿徙平陵

decisions.reason: 陵陽 is Lingyang; “Lingsyang” is a spelling error with no support in the Chinese place name.

decisions.after: During the Jianwu era, one of He Bing's grandsons was appointed a Gentleman.
decisions.reason: The Chinese names only the Jianwu era and identifies the appointee as He Bing's grandson; it does not name Guangwudi.
立定陶王為太子 records the king's establishment as crown prince, while 隆遷 introduces two offices to which Long was promoted.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 上竟立定陶王為太子，隆遷翼州牧、穎川太守

decisions.reason: The replacement restores the accession context, Long as the subject, and 以高第 as the basis for his appointment.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 哀帝即位，以高第入為京兆尹，遷執金吾

decisions.after: At the time, Dong Xian, a Gentleman Attendant, was rising in favor. The emperor ordered palace eunuchs to draw weapons from the imperial arsenal in ten successive deliveries and send them to Dong Xian and the household of the emperor's wet nurse, Wang A.
decisions.reason: 前後十輩 describes ten successive deliveries or groups, not wagonloads; the replacement also restores both occurrences of Dong Xian and Wang A's name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 前後十輩，送董賢及上乳母王阿捨

decisions.reason: The sentence expressly separates the Grand Minister of Agriculture's public funds from maintenance and rewards paid by the Privy Treasurer.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 大司農錢自乘輿不以給共養，共養勞賜，一出少府

decisions.reason: The replacement retains both prohibitions, including the omitted protection of the people's labor, and the stated public-private distinction.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 不以本臧給末用，不以民力共浮費，別公私

decisions.reason: The Chinese gives Long's full analogy between campaign authority, frontier duty, and grants of state weapons; a one-line meta-summary does not translate it.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 漢家邊吏，職在距寇，亦賜武庫兵，皆任其事然後蒙之

decisions.reason: The revision translates the explicit ban on private armor and its purpose without the draft's modern slang.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 家不臧甲，所以抑臣威，損私力也

decisions.reason: The source contrasts public resources and state weapons with favored private households; 'private toys' is unsupported and erases the memorial's direct argument.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以天下公用給其私門，契國威器共其家備

decisions.reason: The replacement restores the diverted labor, furnished weapons, and explicit warning about arrogance and usurpation.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 民力分於弄臣，武兵設於微妾，建立非宜，以廣驕僭

decisions.reason: The Chinese is a direct Confucius quotation about the halls of the Three Families; the draft's Huan arsenals are not present.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 孔子曰：『奚取於三家之堂！』

decisions.reason: The literal requires a complete English question for 奚取於 and a closed quotation.
收還武庫 asks that the issued weapons be recovered and returned to the arsenal.
傅太后 is Empress Dowager Fu, and the sentence distinguishes discounted purchases from the additional taking of eight women from Long's office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 傅太后使謁者買諸官婢，賤取之，復取執金吾官婢八人

decisions.reason: 奏言 and 請 describe a memorial reporting the low price and requesting fair revaluation, not an unspecified demand.
The edict explicitly alleges improper conduct, contentious grasping, a bad official example, and damage to moral instruction and custom.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 舉錯不由誼理，爭求之名自此始，無以示百僚，傷化失俗

claimRetractions.reason: s0224 has only 建武中 and never names 光武帝; the Guangwudi name claim was created solely by the bad idiomatic translation.
With Guangwudi absent from the Chinese of s0224, the ruler-role claim for that invented person has no source support in the repaired unit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 建武中，錄舊德臣，以寶孫伉為諸長

claimRetractions.reason: The polity claim is attached to the Guangwudi person invented from the bad idiomatic; s0224 supports a Jianwu-era court act, not an explicit named emperor subject.
s0301 has only 建武中; the Guangwudi temple-name claim exists solely because the idiomatic invented that name.
No emperor is named in s0301, so the ruler-role claim for the invented Guangwudi person is unsupported.
The male-sex claim depends on the invented Guangwudi person; the Chinese only records a Jianwu-era appointment of Bing’s grandson.

proposals.before: He impeached the heir of General of the Guards Zhang Anshi—Pengzu, gentleman attendant at court and marquis of Yangdu—for failing to dismount at the palace hall gate, and linked the charge to Anshi's occupying office without real benefit.
proposals.after: He impeached the son of General of the Guards Zhang Anshi—Pengzu, gentleman attendant at court and marquis of Yangdu—for failing to dismount at the palace hall gate, and linked the charge to Anshi's occupying office without real benefit.
proposals.reason: Chinese 子 identifies Pengzu as Zhang Anshi son, not his heir.

proposals.before: Before Kuangrao, the guard colonel had to kowtow to the commandant of guards and was treated like a messenger boy for shopping runs.
proposals.after: Earlier, the guard colonel had to kowtow to the commandant of guards and was treated like a messenger boy for shopping runs.
proposals.reason: 先是時 marks the previous custom, not a clause meaning before Kuangrao as a person.

proposals.before: The marquis of Wei laughed and said, "Cigong is mad while sober—what need of wine?"
proposals.after: Chancellor Marquis of Wei laughed and said, "Cigong is mad while sober—what need of wine?"
proposals.reason: Chinese 丞相魏侯 names the speaker as chancellor as well as marquis.

proposals.before: He thanked the emperor for a letter from Master of Reading Yao: the censor must praise good and punish evil, not seize every case.
proposals.after: He thanked the emperor for a letter from Master of Writing Yao: the censor must praise good and punish evil, not seize every case.
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is prefect of the masters of writing; Reading contradicts the Chinese and the literal English.

proposals.before: I only fear there will be no cloud-bank of help, that I will be thrust aside by a crowd of wicked men, letting slanderers succeed, blocking the road of the straight, disheartening loyal ministers and sealing wise men's mouths—this is what your foolish subject fears."
proposals.after: I only fear there will be no help even in the least, that I will be thrust aside by a crowd of wicked men, letting slanderers succeed, blocking the road of the straight, disheartening loyal ministers and sealing wise men's mouths—this is what your foolish subject fears."
proposals.reason: 雲補 means even a slight remedy or help (云 = 有), not a meteorological cloud-bank.

proposals.before: Even Wu and Zhou trembled at small omens, he argued—how much more should a childless age fear heaven's warnings.
proposals.after: Formerly King Wu and the Duke of Zhou, even after receiving the fish-and-crow omens, still trembled and warned one another—how much more should a childless age fear heaven's warnings.
proposals.reason: 武王 and 周公 are King Wu and the Duke of Zhou, not a fused Wu and Zhou, and the received omens are omitted.

proposals.before: Thereupon Left General Xin Qingji, Right General Lian Bao, Chamberlain for Ceremonies Shi Dan, and Palace Grandee Gu Yong jointly submitted a memorial saying, "We have heard that an enlightened king extends a tolerant hearing, honors the offices of remonstrance and dispute, opens wide the path for loyal and upright men, and does not punish reckless or uncompromising words. Only then can the hundred officials in office exhaust their loyalty and offer all their plans without fearing later disaster; the court has no flatterers, and the sovereign has no guides who would lead him from the Way.
proposals.after: Thereupon Left General Xin Qingji, Right General Lian Bao, Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison Shi Dan, and Palace Grandee Gu Yong jointly submitted a memorial saying, "We have heard that an enlightened king extends a tolerant hearing, honors the offices of remonstrance and dispute, opens wide the path for loyal and upright men, and does not punish reckless or uncompromising words. Only then can the hundred officials in office exhaust their loyalty and offer all their plans without fearing later disaster; the court has no flatterers, and the sovereign has no guides who would lead him from the Way.
proposals.reason: 光祿勳 is the palace-garrison chamberlain, not Chamberlain for Ceremonies.

proposals.before: Thereupon Left General Xin Qingji, Right General Lian Bao, Chamberlain for Ceremonies Shi Dan, and Grandee of the Palace Gu Yong jointly submitted a memorial saying, "We have heard that an enlightened king extends a tolerant ear, honors remonstrance officers, opens wide the road of loyalty and uprightness, and does not punish wild or blunt words—then the hundred officials hold their posts, exhaust loyalty and counsel, fear no later disaster, the court has no flatterers, and the sovereign has no guide who would lead him to lose the Way.
proposals.after: Thereupon Left General Xin Qingji, Right General Lian Bao, Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison Shi Dan, and Grandee of the Palace Gu Yong jointly submitted a memorial saying, "We have heard that an enlightened king extends a tolerant ear, honors remonstrance officers, opens wide the road of loyalty and uprightness, and does not punish wild or blunt words—then the hundred officials hold their posts, exhaust loyalty and counsel, fear no later disaster, the court has no flatterers, and the sovereign has no guide who would lead him to lose the Way.
proposals.reason: Same office error in the literal field: 光祿勳 is not Ceremonies.

proposals.before: One was the Zhao empress's father—
proposals.after: The Marquis of Kongxiang is the empress's father;
proposals.reason: The Chinese names 孔鄉侯 as the empress's father and does not say Zhao.

proposals.before: Ai recalled him to censor, then metropolitan governor.
proposals.after: When Emperor Ai ascended the throne, Bao was summoned as Grandee Remonstrant and promoted to Colonel Director of the Retainers.
proposals.reason: 司隸 is the metropolitan commandant (Colonel Director of the Retainers), not the Jingzhao metropolitan governor already named at s0170.

proposals.before: Sun Bao sent a chancellor's investigator, exposed the fraud, and impeached Li and Shang for deceiving the throne.
proposals.after: Sun Bao sent a chancellor's investigator, exposed the fraud, and impeached Wang Li and Li Shang for deceiving the throne.
proposals.reason: Chinese 立、尚 are Wang Li and Li Shang; bare Li/Shang collides with Li Shang's surname.

proposals.before: Li was not punished, but later when his elder brother Shang, Grand Marshal and General of the Guards, died, Li should have succeeded him next; the emperor passed over Li and appointed his younger brother Gen, Marquis of Quyang, Grand Marshal and Cavalry General.
proposals.after: Wang Li was not punished, but later when his elder brother Shang, Grand Marshal and General of the Guards, died, Wang Li should have succeeded him next; the emperor passed over Wang Li and appointed his younger brother Gen, Marquis of Quyang, Grand Marshal and Cavalry General.
proposals.reason: 立 is Wang Li, not Li Shang who has just died in prison in the previous sentence.

proposals.before: When the memorial was submitted, the Son of Heaven was displeased. Because Bao was a noted minister, he could not bear to execute him, and therefore issued a formal edict to the chancellor and Grand Minister of Works: "Metropolitan Commandant Bao has memorialized that the former Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Chong was wronged, and asks that Master of Writing Zhao Chang be imprisoned and tried.
proposals.after: When the memorial was submitted, the Son of Heaven was displeased. Because Bao was a noted minister, he could not bear to execute him, and therefore issued a formal edict to the chancellor and Grand Minister of Works: "Director of Retainers Bao has memorialized that the former Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Chong was wronged, and asks that Master of Writing Chang be imprisoned and tried.
proposals.reason: The edict names 司隸寶 and 尚書令昌; metropolitan governor/Zhao are not in the Chinese of this unit.

proposals.before: It happened that Yuegui commandery reported a yellow dragon swimming in the river; Grand Tutor Kong Guang, grand minister of works Ma Gong, and others all praised Wang Mang's merit and virtue as comparable to the Duke of Zhou and said it should be announced at the ancestral temple.
proposals.after: It happened that Yuegui commandery reported a yellow dragon swimming in the river; Grand Tutor Kong Guang, Grand Minister of Education Ma Gong, and others all praised Wang Mang's merit and virtue as comparable to the Duke of Zhou and said it should be announced at the ancestral temple.
proposals.reason: 大司徒 is the Chancellor/Minister of Education, not Grand Minister of Works (大司空).

proposals.before: Wang Mang recalled him to greet the boy emperor.
proposals.after: When Emperor Ai died, Wang Mang reported to Queen Mother Wang and summoned Bao as Grandee of the Palace to welcome the King of Zhongshan together with Wang Shun and others.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence omits Emperor Ai's death, Queen Mother Wang, the 光祿大夫 appointment, Wang Shun, and the King of Zhongshan, and invents a boy emperor.

proposals.before: Grand Minister of Agriculture funds are not taken from the imperial carriage for allowances; allowances and gifts for support all come from the privy treasury.
proposals.after: Even the imperial establishment is not supplied for its maintenance from Grand Minister of Agriculture funds; maintenance and rewards for service all come from the Privy Treasurer.
proposals.reason: The literal reverses 大司農錢自乘輿不以給共養: Da Sinong funds are not used even for the emperor's keep, which comes from the Shaofu.

proposals.before: Mang cashiered Shi Li, Ding Xuan, and Zhao Chang to Hepu.
proposals.after: Shi Li was then Palace Grand Coachman, Ding Xuan administrator of Taishan, and Zhao Chang—the Prefect of the Masters of Writing who had slandered Zheng Chong—administrator of Henei; all were dismissed from office and relocated to Hepu.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops the offices, omits Zheng Chong, and invents Mang as grammatical subject.

proposals.before: Chengdi's mother wept to Ai for Wang Linqing.
proposals.after: The empress dowager of Emperor Cheng, because the Empress Dowager of Qiongcheng loved Linqing, wept when she heard of it and spoke to Emperor Ai.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line omits 以邛成太后愛林卿故 and compresses 聞之涕泣，為言哀帝.

proposals.before: He took Yingchuan from the mild magistrate Yan Xu.
proposals.after: He was transferred to governor of Yingchuan, replacing Yan Xu of Lingyang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 徙穎川太守，代陵陽嚴詡 is a transfer into the Yingchuan governorship replacing Yan Xu of Lingyang; 陵陽 is a place-name, and 代 means replacement rather than taking the commandery from him.

decisions.reason: 張安世子 names Pengzu as Anshi's son; 子 is not a designated heir.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 張安世子侍中陽都侯彭祖

decisions.reason: After Kuangrao is made 衛司馬, 先是時 naturally marks the office's prior custom; naming him as the time-anchor is accurate enough, and Earlier is only a style swap.

decisions.after: The chancellor, the Marquis of Wei, laughed and said, "Cigong is mad while sober—what need of wine?"
decisions.reason: 丞相魏侯 names both the chancellorship and the Wei marquisate; the original drops 丞相, but Chancellor Marquis of Wei is awkward English.
尚書令堯 is a master of writing, not of reading.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 使尚書令堯賜臣豐書曰

decisions.reason: 未有雲補 means not even the slightest remedy or help; 雲 is not a bank of clouds.
武王、周公 are King Wu and the Duke of Zhou, and 魚烏之瑞 are auspicious omens they had already received, not fused Wu and Zhou trembling at small omens.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 昔武王、周公承順天地，以饗魚烏之瑞

decisions.reason: 光祿勳 is the palace-garrison chamberlain, not Chamberlain for Ceremonies (太常).
The same 光祿勳 title is not the ceremonial chamberlaincy.
孔鄉侯，皇后父 names the Marquis of Kongxiang as the empress's father and does not mention a Zhao empress.
諫大夫 is grandee remonstrant and 司隸 is the retainers' commandant, not a Jingzhao metropolitan governor.
立、尚 are Wang Li of Hongyang and administrator Li Shang; Li and Shang wrongly gives Wang Li the surname Li.
立雖不坐 continues Wang Li after 尚下獄死; bare Li would confuse him with Li Shang.

decisions.after: When the memorial was submitted, the Son of Heaven was displeased. Because Bao was a noted minister, he could not bear to execute him, and therefore issued a formal edict to the chancellor and Grand Minister of Works: "Metropolitan Commandant Bao has memorialized that the former Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Chong was wronged, and asks that Master of Writing Chang be imprisoned and tried.
decisions.reason: 尚書令昌 does not supply the surname Zhao, so that addition should drop; 司隸寶 is already well rendered as Metropolitan Commandant, and Director of Retainers is only a style swap.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 司隸寶奏故尚書僕射崇冤，請獄治尚書令昌

decisions.after: It happened that Yuegui commandery reported a yellow dragon swimming in the river; Grand Preceptor Kong Guang, Grand Minister of Education Ma Gong, and others all praised Wang Mang's merit and virtue as comparable to the Duke of Zhou and said it should be announced at the ancestral temple.
decisions.reason: 大司徒 is Grand Minister of Education, not Works (大司空); the proposal still renders 太師 as Grand Tutor, which is 太傅.
哀帝崩…白王太后徵寶以為光祿大夫，與王舜等俱迎中山王 names Ai's death, the queen mother, the appointment, Wang Shun, and the King of Zhongshan; boy emperor is invented.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 哀帝崩，王莽白王太后徵寶以為光祿大夫，與王舜等俱迎中山王

decisions.reason: 大司農錢自乘輿不以給共養 means even the emperor's keep is not paid from Da Sinong funds; the original reverses the source and the beneficiary.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 大司農錢自乘輿不以給共養，共養勞賜，一出少府

decisions.reason: The sentence lists Shi Li, Ding Xuan, and Zhao Chang with offices and Zheng Chong, then 皆免官，徙合浦; it does not make Mang the subject.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 史立時為中太僕，丁玄奏山太守，及尚書令趙昌譖鄭崇者為河內太守，皆免官，徙合浦

decisions.reason: 成帝太后 weeps and speaks to Ai because 邛成太后愛林卿; the original drops that cause and the hearing.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 成帝太后以邛成太后愛林卿故，聞之涕泣，為言哀帝

decisions.reason: 徙穎川太守，代陵陽嚴詡 is a transfer replacing Yan Xu of Lingyang; 陵陽 is a place-name, not mild, and 代 is succession, not seizure.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 徙穎川太守，代陵陽嚴詡

claimRevisions.reason: 太師 is the Grand Preceptor, not the Grand Tutor (太傅); the English office label followed the unrevised literal.
